column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-container.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS. pleme-container is a tier-2 family composer: it holds no
# logic of its own, only a two-arm dispatch on `inputs.target` into
# image-push.yml and vendor-image-mirror.yml. Its entire contract is therefore a
# SELECTION contract — exactly the thing a unit test cannot see and actionlint
# will not read. The rows below assert that the two arms are mutually exclusive
# (a broken `==` that matched both would double-dispatch a push AND a mirror
# from one call) and that each arm is genuinely reachable (a typo'd literal
# would make its job `NEVER`, which looks identical to a job that works).
# BOTH JOBS PUSH BYTES SOMEWHERE — this is not a table over harmless work.
# `image-push` builds and pushes an image; `vendor-image-mirror` copies a vendor
# image into our registry. So each row states which of the two publishing acts
# is INTENDED for that input, and the two non-matching rows below state that
# NEITHER is intended. A regression that made both arms fire would publish an
# unrequested artifact while the run stayed green.
# THE AXIS AND ITS BOUNDARIES. `inputs.target` is the only context path any
# condition in this file reads, so the axis is total: one row per named arm,
# plus the two boundary rows that would otherwise rot.
#   * `unknown-target` — a real reusable name from a DIFFERENT family. This
#     workflow has NO catch-all job, so an unrecognised target selects nothing
#     and the run reports success having dispatched no work. That is a finding
#     about the workflow, recorded here rather than papered over: the row pins
#     today's behaviour (both arms quiet) so that if a catch-all is ever added,
#     this row goes red and forces the new job to be asserted instead of
#     acquired silently.
#   * `empty-target` — `target: ""`. GitHub's `required: true` enforces that the
#     key is PRESENT, never that it is non-empty, and pleme.yml passes the value
#     straight through as `target: "${{ inputs.target }}"`, so a caller
#     interpolating an unset variable lands here with the empty string. "the
#     caller computed nothing" is a distinct state from any named target and is
#     exactly where a catch-all added later would need to catch.
# WHY THE TWO BOUNDARY ROWS ARE REACHABLE AT ALL, given pleme.yml validates.
# pleme.yml's `validate` job greps this very file for `inputs.target == '<t>'`
# and fails an unknown target before `container` runs — so on the pleme.yml
# path, rows 3 and 4 are unreachable. But this workflow's own header states it
# is directly callable ("Calling it directly also works and simply spends one
# fewer chain level"), and on THAT path there is no validate job in front of it.
# The boundary rows cover the unguarded entry point, which is the one where a
# green-over-nothing run is possible.
# WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT SEE. Both arms are `uses:` dispatches. This linter
# models dispatch only and never descends into the called workflow's own
# conditions — image-push.yml has its own `resolve-runner`/`push` pair and
# vendor-image-mirror.yml its own `mirror` job, each with gates of their own.
# "image-push ran" here means "the reusable was invoked", never "an image was
# pushed". Those two workflows need their own tables; this one does not cover
# them.
# Arm 1. The push family's build-and-push leaf is dispatched; the mirror stays
# quiet. INTENDED PUBLISH: an image push, and nothing else.
image-push
# Arm 2. The vendor mirror is dispatched; the push stays quiet. INTENDED
# PUBLISH: a vendor-image mirror, and nothing else.
vendor-image-mirror
# Boundary: a target this composer does not serve. `cargo-ci` is a real
# catalogued reusable — one of the nine that nest and are dispatched directly
# from pleme.yml — so this is the realistic mistype/mis-route, not a fictional
# string. INTENDED PUBLISH: none. Today no job selects and the run is green
# having done nothing; see the header for why that is recorded rather than
# asserted away.
unknown-target
# Boundary: the caller supplied an empty string (an unset variable interpolated
# through pleme.yml's `with: { target: "${{ inputs.target }}" }`). Distinct from
# any named target and from a missing key. INTENDED PUBLISH: none.
empty-target
